opening.argument: The presentation explains the differences among piles, anal fissure, and fistula, identifying their symptoms, causes, and treatment through medical-topic title cards and spoken treatment discussion. It also promotes homeopathic medicines and related consultation services, including a medicine shop and telephonic booking channel, but that promotion remains ordinary medical-treatment advertising. Nothing presented establishes a deceptive payment demand, false credential, investment opportunity, or impersonation mechanism. The material is additionally framed as general guidance and advises viewers to consult a qualified health professional. That disclaimer does not prove the treatment claims are true or clinically effective, but it supports treating the presentation as general medical information with associated services rather than a deceptive scheme.
